newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Jan, Feb health outlays to meet goal - Barrot.
newsitem.headline: French Jan, Feb health outlays to meet goal - Barrot.

text.p: French Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot said on Sunday that health spending in January and February was likely to fall within government-set objectives.
"We are going to see, probably in the middle of the week, the results of January and February spending of the health insurance fund," Barrot told Europe 1 radio in an interview.
"The trend that is starting for the first two months of the year is one that leads us towards a respect of the target the parliament set," he said.
He refused to give precise figures, noting that the data would be officially released by the CNAM national health insurance fund, but said the year was starting out well.
"I have reason to believe the trend is positive," he said.
In 1996, non-hospital spending in France rose 2.3 percent, more than the 2.1 percent targeted by the government.
France's parliament has targeted a rise of 1.7 percent in total spending on public health in 1997. Spending on doctors fees and prescriptions is to rise no more than 1.3 percent.
